html:
The global order faces significant instability as US-Iran tensions intensify, with Iran warning of potential attacks on US military targets in Europe amidst President Trump's "economic war" and declaration of the Strait of Hormuz as "new US territory." This comes as the US national debt has surged past $40 trillion for the first time, fueling debate over the country's economic stability and geopolitical priorities.

Russia-Ukraine: Ukraine is grappling with air defense shortages following a "massive attack" on Kyiv that killed at least 15 people and targeted blocks of flats and warehouses. Meanwhile, a marine drone was destroyed by a Romanian F-16 fighter jet near the Neptun Deep gas platform in the Black Sea, prompting a warning from the EU’s von der Leyen of an "escalating campaign of threats." Separately, Russia and Ukraine exchanged 103 captured soldiers each in a deal mediated by the UAE.

US Politics & Economy: The US national debt has topped $40 trillion, with some outlets attributing the surge in part to Trump’s invalidated tariffs that forced the government to return tens of billions of dollars. This economic landscape forms the backdrop for ongoing scrutiny of Trump's administration, including questions over aide Natalie Harp's influence and an FBI investigation involving former US representative Eric Swalwell related to sexual assault allegations. Separately, the publisher of the Stars and Stripes military news outlet could face early dismissal after reports on deteriorating conditions aboard a US aircraft carrier.

Middle East: Amidst the rising US-Iran tensions, an Israeli airstrike killed six Palestinians at a police post in Gaza, contributing to a death toll exceeding 73,000 since October 2023. The Israeli military has launched criminal investigations into the killings of 5-year-old Hind Rajab and paramedics, acknowledging for the first time that its troops fired on the car carrying her, though her family has rejected the probe. Concurrently, Kushner reportedly met with Hamas regarding Trump's Gaza plan, as the US plans to provide $206 million for a peacekeeping force in Gaza. Regional complexities further emerged with the head of Mossad reportedly speaking with the Syrian foreign minister before an Israeli airstrike, and the Yemeni government warning of Houthi plans to seize the coast of a key strait.

Europe & Global Affairs: The International Criminal Court has condemned US sanctions against its president and a senior prosecution lawyer as a "flagrant attack" on its independence. In other news from Europe, Prince Harry and Meghan announced a surprise return to the United Kingdom for an extended stay, though not resuming royal duties, a decision that reportedly "blind-sided the royals." Meanwhile, a Belgian car salesman, Clément Vandenkerckhove, became a prince after his royal parentage was confirmed. On the continent's rivers, unusually low water levels due to drought have revealed Nazi shipwrecks in the Danube.

Humanitarian & Security: A humanitarian crisis continues to unfold in Sudan, with over 200,000 people newly displaced in Kordofan as fighting rages. In Africa, a gold mine collapse in the Central African Republic left at least 100 dead, and an Ebola outbreak in Congo reached 5,000 cases, spreading at an unprecedented speed. Elsewhere, more than 1,000 Afghan refugees remain stranded at a camp in Qatar since 2021, while in Liberia, a former vice-president, Jewel Howard-Taylor, was charged in a drug-trafficking probe.
